cadet.gauge.oxygen: The air the crew breathes. If it gets too low, they can't breathe well.
cadet.gauge.co2: The bad air building up. The air cleaner takes it back out.
cadet.gauge.water: How many days of drinking water are left.
cadet.gauge.food: How many days of food are left. Picking crops adds more.
cadet.gauge.battery: How much power is stored up, like a big phone battery for the whole base.
cadet.gauge.cabin: How warm or cold it is inside. Too cold or too hot is bad for everyone.

specialist.gauge.oxygen: Cabin oxygen partial pressure. Below about 120 mmHg the crew is short of breath; the sim tracks this hour by hour, not just the total kg stored.
specialist.gauge.co2: Cabin CO₂ partial pressure. Rises as the crew breathes; the scrubber pulls it back down. The limit shown depends on the current rations mode — a harsher mode tolerates less.
specialist.gauge.water: Potable water on hand, shown as days of supply for the living crew at the current recovery rate.
specialist.gauge.food: Stored dry food mass, shown as days of supply at the current ration. Crops add to this when they're harvested.
specialist.gauge.battery: Stored electrical energy. Generation below demand draws this down; sustained zero means load shedding.
specialist.gauge.cabin: Habitat air temperature. Too cold risks hypothermia and frozen water lines; too hot stresses the crew and the equipment bay.

commander.gauge.oxygen: pO₂, cabin. Hypoxic risk below ~120 mmHg (S1.1); tracked continuously, independent of the O₂ mass stored.
commander.gauge.co2: pCO₂, cabin. Production scales with crew metabolic rate; scrubber uptime and efficiency set the removal side. Limit is mode-dependent (survivalModes' own co2LimitMmHg).
commander.gauge.water: Potable reserve, expressed as days of supply at current per-crew consumption and recovery-loop efficiency.
commander.gauge.food: Dry mass reserve, expressed as days of supply at the current ration's kcal/crew-day. Harvests are a real, tracked inflow.
commander.gauge.battery: State of charge. A sustained generation/demand deficit forces the load-shed priority order (Power console) to shed systems bottom-up.
commander.gauge.cabin: Habitat air temperature, thermostat-controlled. Drives the hypothermia clock below 15 °C and equipment/crew heat stress at the high end.
